From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Issues Review (Seller Draft, Data Room as at 22 Sept 2026)

**Priority items:** SPA-N-008 (Bluefen), SPA-N-009 (Riverlark), SPA-N-012 (privacy incident), SPA-N-011 (Ironquay), SPA-N-010 (bonuses), and the knowledge and disclosure provisions (SPA-N-006/007). These can cost the Buyer real money and should be resolved before signing, not left to the general warranty regime.

**Caveats:**
- The data room cut-off is 22 September 2026, and today is 5 November 2026. Confirm the current status of every item below.
- I have reviewed the Seller's summary of the SPA, not the full draft. Check the clause references against the actual document.
- Confirm the NSW and Australian law points with local counsel. The Australian Consumer Law and privacy points in particular need specialist review.

---

## Caps, thresholds and time limits

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** Aggregate cap of 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims.
- **Buyer should want:** Cap at 100% of price (AUD 24m) for general warranties. Fallback is no less than 50% (AUD 12m), given the known issues in the disclosure letter.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** A 20% cap leaves the Buyer exposed on a debt-free/cash-free deal with several known material issues.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket**
- **Seller:** AUD 25,000 de minimis per claim. AUD 250,000 deductible basket, with only the excess recoverable.
- **Buyer should want:** De minimis of about AUD 10,000, with related claims aggregated. A tipping basket of about 1% of price (AUD 240,000), so that once it is exceeded the Buyer recovers from the first dollar.
- **Recommendation: Counter.** A true deductible means the Buyer bears the first AUD 250,000 of any warranty loss, and the known AUD 330,000 Sandbar renewals alone would exceed that.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months from Completion for all Claims, with the limit applying to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer should want:** 36 months for general warranties. Tax claims run until 60 days after the relevant ATO assessment period closes. Fundamental claims run for at least 6 years.
- **Recommendation: Counter.** 18 months is short for a sale involving unresolved consents, a privacy investigation and an open IP payment, and some issues will not surface within that period.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties.
- **Buyer should want:** Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority) capped at the full price, with a limitation period of at least 6 years.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** Title is the core of what the Buyer is paying for, and it should not sit under a 20% cap and 18-month limit.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** No fraud carve-out. Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply the limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions to "all Claims of any nature."
- **Buyer should want:** An express carve-out for fraud from the caps, time limits, exclusive remedy, non-reliance and knowledge provisions. Non-reliance clauses also generally cannot exclude misleading or deceptive conduct under the Australian Consumer Law, so this should be confirmed with counsel.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** The current drafting would protect the Seller even from its own fraud.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** A single regime for all Claims, to be "administratively simple."
- **Buyer should want:** Separate regimes for general warranties, fundamental warranties, tax warranties and tax indemnity, specific indemnities (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses, privacy incident, Sandbar if needed) and fraud.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** Known risks need specific indemnities, which the general regime cannot deliver.

---

## Disclosure and knowledge

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** Clauses 1.1 and 1.2 disclose "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the data room (DD-002 to DD-012), plus the Accounts, statutory registers and public records.
- **Buyer should want:** Specific disclosure only, against specifically identified warranties, meeting a fair disclosure standard. No general data room disclosure. Disclosure should not qualify fundamental warranties or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** General data room disclosure would qualify almost every warranty, leaving the Buyer with no practical warranty claim.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** Clause 8.3 bars claims for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew about, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer should want:** Delete clause 8.3. Include an express pro-sandbagging clause, so that the Buyer's knowledge does not defeat a warranty claim. Known matters should be covered by specific indemnities, not warranties.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** The Buyer has now read the disclosed issues, and this clause would turn that knowledge into a defence for the Seller.

---

## Specific issues

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** Clauses 3 and 6.3. The Seller will use "reasonable endeavours" and treat consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. The data room contains no final written consent and no evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are met. Bluefen accounts for about AUD 3.6m (about 30%) of FY26 revenue.
- **Buyer should want:** Bluefen's written consent, in agreed form and with the clause 11.3 conditions satisfied, as a hard condition precedent. The Buyer keeps a right to waive it. The Seller bears the cost of satisfying the conditions. If consent is refused or terminated after Completion, a specific indemnity or price adjustment applies, or part of the price is held in escrow.
- **Recommendation: Reject "reasonable endeavours."** The Buyer cannot control whether Bluefen consents, so an endeavours obligation transfers that risk to the Buyer.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** Clauses 2 and 7. About AUD 3.2m outstanding, to be "addressed by a release to be provided following Completion." The facility has not been repaid, and no discharge of security is in the data room.
- **Buyer should want:** A payoff letter and discharge of all security (including PPSR releases) delivered at Completion. The payoff amount, plus accrued interest and break costs, is paid from the price under the cash-free/debt-free mechanics. Any undischarged security is a condition precedent.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** A post-Completion release would leave the Buyer owning a company with a live AUD 3.2m secured facility, and the Buyer would have paid the Seller for it.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** Disclosure letter section 5 records AUD 420,000 of conditional Completion bonuses (DD-005). The Seller says these are "a matter for the Seller" and are not in the draft funds flow. The disclosure does not say whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.
- **Buyer should want:** The bonuses, plus all associated payroll tax, superannuation guarantee and on-costs, treated as transaction-related debt-like items deducted from the price, or paid by the Seller at or before Completion. A specific indemnity for all change-of-control employee entitlements.
- **Recommendation: Reject exclusion from the funds flow.** Amounts payable by the company after Completion are the Buyer's cost unless they are priced in, and the on-costs are currently unquantified.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** Clause 11.1. The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "considered adequate." DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open. Under DD-004 clause 7.3, SOW3 Project Materials do not transfer until every SOW3 fee is paid. No receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.
- **Buyer should want:** Proof of payment of the AUD 180,000 and a confirmatory assignment of the SOW3 Project Materials before Completion. Failing that, the AUD 180,000 is held in escrow or retention, plus a buffer. The IP indemnity extends to all Ironquay claims and to any defect in title to the Project Materials, and sits alongside a separate IP warranty.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** The company may not own the materials it is relying on until the open fees are paid, and the Seller's indemnity does not address that.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident**
- **Seller:** Clause 4.6 and Schedule 6. The Seller calls the DD-006 matter "preliminary" and "not expected to be material." Disclosure letter section 6 says the export may contain about 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps), and that it is not known whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required.
- **Buyer should want:** A completed forensic investigation before signing, or a pre-Completion covenant to complete it. A specific privacy indemnity covering notification costs, regulator action, third-party claims and remediation, with a separate cap or uncapped. A privacy compliance warranty. An escrow or retention until the investigation is complete. The Buyer should also check whether the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) applies to Paperbark, and whether the assessment window is running.
- **Recommendation: Reject "not expected to be material."** The record is unresolved, and the Seller's characterisation is not supported by the disclosure letter's own description.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate), described as ordinary-course operating costs. The disclosure says it is not known whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Buyer should want:** The contracts, with term, termination rights and commitments. Confirmation of whether the renewals are related, since reading them together gives a larger total. Any multi-year or non-terminable commitment outside the normal working-capital cycle treated as debt-like or priced in. Accurate cost recognition in the completion accounts.
- **Recommendation: Counter.** Accept as ordinary course only if the contracts show 12-month, terminable terms within normal operations. Otherwise, treat the commitments as debt-like.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title to 100% of the shares is "evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012." The disclosure letter says this does not confirm the Buyer has verified title itself.
- **Buyer should want:** An independent ASIC company extract, the original share certificates, a full transfer history, a PPSR search over the shares, and confirmation that no options, liens or other encumbrances exist. A fundamental title warranty. Delivery of executed transfer documents as a completion deliverable.
- **Recommendation: Verify before signing.** The Seller's source is a company register, which is the Seller's own document and is not independent verification.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions are "settled under the general regime above."
- **Buyer should want:** Full tax warranties and a pre-Completion tax indemnity, with a longer limitation period, separate from the general cap. IP warranties covering ownership, non-infringement and sufficiency of rights, including for the Ironquay Project Materials, with separate limits.
- **Recommendation: Reject "settled."** Neither position has been negotiated, and both depend on the general regime the Buyer is rejecting.

---

**Immediate next steps:** Send the Seller a markup rejecting clauses 8.3, 9.3, 12.8, 20.5 and 1.1/1.2. Request the Bluefen consent, Riverlark payoff letter, Ironquay payment evidence, the privacy investigation status and the Sandbar contracts. Confirm the current data room position, since the disclosure letter is about six weeks old.
